title: Weights that can run code: pickle, safetensors, torch.load

questions.q: Why can loading a .ckpt run code?
options: It is usually a pickle, and a pickle can call functions when rebuilt
Safetensors converts it to a program
questions.answer: It is usually a pickle, and a pickle can call functions when rebuilt
questions.why: The Python docs warn about exactly this.

questions.q: What does load_torch_file do with a .pt file at v0.43.0?
questions.why: Read in comfy/utils.py. The lab's payload is refused on this path.

questions.q: Why doesn't core's protection cover everything?
options: Packs can call their own loaders
questions.answer: Packs can call their own loaders
questions.why: Core's choice doesn't bind a pack. Search it for pickle.load and weights_only=False.

questions.q: A file named model.safetensors starts with PK. What should you think?
options: The name is wrong, and it looks like a zip from torch.save
It is a normal safetensors file
It is safe because of the name
questions.answer: The name is wrong, and it looks like a zip from torch.save
questions.why: The first bytes tell you more than the name does.

questions.q: A file is refused by weights_only=True. What is the right response?
options: Find a safetensors copy, or inspect it in isolation
Set weights_only=False to make it load
questions.answer: Find a safetensors copy, or inspect it in isolation
questions.why: The refusal means it wants more than weights.

questions.answer: Runs Python from the model's repository
